乔治·拉塞尔在第二轮练习中领跑皮埃尔·加斯利的阿尔法罗密欧车队，因为第一天的赛道练习湿滑，几乎没有进行多少运行；在天空体育F1频道观看拉斯维加斯大奖赛，周六凌晨4点进行排位赛，周日凌晨4点进行比赛
周五拉斯维加斯大奖赛练习赛的亮点
在拉斯维加斯大奖赛的第一天赛道练习中，梅赛德斯车队的乔治·拉塞尔在第二轮练习中领跑阿尔法罗密欧车队的皮埃尔·加斯利，因为雨限制了赛道运行。
由于第一场练习赛因大雨持续，没有完成计时圈数，天气最终放晴，允许在第二场练习赛中进行了大量的跑圈，尽管是在潮湿、逐渐干燥的赛道上，这阻止了使用干胎。
在周四晚上的拉斯维加斯进行的练习赛结束时，最佳圈速出现，拉塞尔以0.071秒的优势超过了加斯利，法拉利的查尔斯·勒克莱尔落后三分之十，排在第三。

诺里斯最终排名第七，落后于红牛的伊萨克·哈德贾，他的麦克拉伦队友奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里和法拉利的刘易斯·汉密尔顿，但鉴于排位赛和比赛预计将在干燥条件下进行，这些成绩可能意义不大。
拉斯维加斯的赛程比传统的F1周末提前一天，但时差意味着对于英国观众来说，排位赛将在周六早上4点进行，比赛将在同一天的同一时间进行。

令人惊讶的是，整个比赛日中事故很少，唯一的一次红旗是在第二次练习赛高速弯道处，一个塑料袋被吹到了赛道上

皮亚斯蒂、威廉姆斯的卡洛斯·塞恩斯和阿斯顿·马丁的兰斯·斯特罗尔因为超过各种动力单元部件，将受到十位的发车线处罚，而哈斯车队的奥利弗·贝尔曼将从最后一位发车
红牛车队的马克斯·维斯塔潘在拉斯维加斯大奖赛的第一场练习赛中与雨水搏斗
马克斯·维斯塔潘大部分时间都在维修区，总共完成了10圈，以第13名的成绩完成了第二场练习赛
维斯塔潘目前正处于连续八次登上领奖台的状态，他感觉在完成的圈数中引擎"没有动力"，尽管他的工程师建议问题可能与需要适应寒冷天气的引擎动力单元有关，但他坚持认为"这不是正常的"

最终练习将在周六凌晨12:30开始，对于英国观众来说，这将是一个非常忙碌的时刻，因为车手们将试图在资格赛之前完成尽可能多的干燥圈数。

detailEn: Las Vegas GP: George Russell tops practice for Mercedes as rain limits running on first day of track action

George Russell topped second practice from Pierre Gasly after there was very little running in first practice on a wet first day on track action; watch the Las Vegas GP on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 4am on Saturday and the race at 4am on Sunday
Highlights from Friday's practice sessions at the Las Vegas Grand Prix
Mercedes' George Russell topped Practice Two from Alpine's Pierre Gasly as rain limited running on the opening day of track action at the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

After no timed laps were completed in first practice due to heavy rain falling throughout, the weather relented to allow plenty of running during the second session, albeit on a damp, slowly drying circuit that prevented the use of slick tyres.

The best lap times came at the end of the session, which took place on Thursday night in Las Vegas, when Russell pipped Gasly by 0.071s, with Ferrari's Charles Leclerc three tenths off the pace in third.

Leclerc and McLaren's Lando Norris, who won last time out in Brazil, had traded the fastest times for most of the session in the wetter conditions.

Norris ended up seventh, behind Red Bull's Isack Hadjar, his McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, but the times are likely to matter very little given qualifying and the race are expected to take place in dry conditions.

The schedule in Las Vegas runs a day earlier than a traditional F1 weekend, but the time difference means qualifying will take place at 4am on Saturday morning for UK viewers, with race following at the same time on Sunday.
Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins and Anthony Davidson run through McLaren and Mercedes' new upgrades they're bringing to the Las Vegas GP
Remarkably, there were few incidents and the only red flag across the whole day was for a plastic bag blowing onto the circuit at the high-speed final corner in second practice.
New F1 world champion Kimi Antonelli was eighth fastest but will serve a five-place grid penalty after exceeding his internal combustion engine allocation for a second time this season.
Piastri, Williams' Carlos Sainz and Aston Martin's Lance Stroll have 10-place grid penalties for going over various power unit elements, while Haas' Oliver Bearman will start at the back.
Red Bull's Max Verstappen battles the rain during the first practice session at the Las Vegas GP
Max Verstappen spent most of the day in the garage and completed only 10 laps in total as he finished second practice in 13th.

Verstappen, who is on a run of eight consecutive podiums, felt he had "no power" from the engine on the laps he completed and insisted "it was not normal" despite his engineer suggesting the issue was related to the power unit needing to warm up in the cold condtions.

McLaren and Mercedes have brought upgrades this weekend but the rain on Friday meant it was virtually impossible to tell whether they made any impact.
Final practice, which gets under way at 12.30am on Saturday for UK viewers, is set to be very busy as the drivers will attempt to get plenty of dry laps in before qualifying.

detailEn: Qatar GP Qualifying: George Russell bounces back with superb performance to beat Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position

George Russell beats Kimi Antonelli to pole as Mercedes seal dominant one-two; Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri on second row; Isack Hadjar beats Max Verstappen to fifth; watch the Qatar Grand Prix live on Sky Sports F1 at 4pm on Sunday, with build-up from 2.30pm
George Russell took pole position in Qatar as Kimi Antonelli seemed unhappy with his lap during qualifying
George Russell produced a superb performance in Qatar Grand Prix Qualifying to beat his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position.

The reignition of Russell's feud with Max Verstappen at last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix had dominated the build-up to the penultimate race of the season, but the Brit produced the perfect response as he topped all three parts of qualifying.

That came as a surprise after Antonelli, who sealed the drivers' title with four rounds to spare, had topped all three practice sessions, but the Italian was unable to match Russell when it mattered most.

Verstappen, who said after winning in Las Vegas last weekend that Russell is "far below" his level, was beaten to fifth by his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar.
Charles Leclerc took seventh but his Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton was beaten to eighth by Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad, with the latter's team-mate Liam Lawson completing the top ten.

Mercedes' dominance is a surprise as nearly every race following August's summer break has been very competitive at the front but it seems a combination of the smooth, high-speed track layout and Mercedes finally getting on top of their upgrades from a month ago has given them a significant margin on their rivals.
"Mercedes are almost in a class of their own, so it's worth the rest looking at the gap to Verstappen [in third]," said Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins.

Ferrari had a difficult Friday after a spin for Charles Leclerc and an engine issue for Lewis Hamilton, but Leclerc fared better in final practice in fifth, ahead of McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.
Hamilton was unhappy throughout the session and stated his "car won't turn" after his final flying lap which put him in ninth, in between Racing Bulls duo Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson.
